hook: In nineteen sixty-two, a man lived in a cave without clocks. He lost twenty-five days.
twist: Michel Siffre spent two months 130 m underground with no clock or sun. Counting to 120 took him five minutes; when his team ended the experiment on 14 September he thought it was 20 August. Yet his body kept a near-daily rhythm (about 24 h 30 min). Harvard later showed cave lamps had reset the clocks in such experiments; measured properly, the brain's clock runs 24 hours 11 minutes, and light sets it.
angle: The Brain loses track of the days, but the body's clock never stops; just before the clocks go back. Big number: 25 days lost; 24 h 11 min.
why_now: Clocks change: UK 25 Oct, US 1 Nov 2026; publish 28 Oct. Scout 2026-10-06 (query 'brain facts'): median of the top 25 is 10.8M, with sleep Shorts like 'Why We Feel Sleepy While Studying' at 19.3M.
risks: Siffre is a real person: named, never drawn (a tent, a lamp, a phone line).
The 25 days and the 24 h 30 min cycle are his own account; label it.
